analysis.title: "Not Yet Negative Enough": Goldman's Risk Gauge Breaks Below Zero, But Contrarian Buy Signal Is Still A Long Way Off
key_insights: Goldman's cross-asset Risk Appetite Indicator (RAI) fell to -0.5 last week, its lowest since April 2025 (Liberation Day tariff crash). It was above +1 in late summer, a drop of about 1.5 points in a couple of months.
Goldman says readings below -1, and especially near -2, have historically been useful contrarian buy signals. The current level is not negative enough to send that signal.

The correlation between the RAI and Nasdaq 100 performance vs the equal-weight S&P 500 has climbed to almost 1 over two weeks. The 1-year correlation is the highest since 2020. Cross-asset risk appetite is now effectively a proxy for the AI trade.

Credit did most of the damage to the RAI, dragging the PC1 'Global growth' factor. The bond rally propped up the PC2 'Monetary policy' factor. Goldman's credit risk appetite gauge is near -3, below its April 2025 trough, while the equity gauge has only just slipped below zero.

Credit excess returns saw another multi-standard-deviation sell-off. EUR IG excess returns fell more than 5 standard deviations on the week, EUR HY over 4, and French 10Y about 2 (chart readings approximate). G4 10-year bonds rallied, with Japan, US, UK and German 10Ys the top performers.

Euro Area-exposed assets underperformed their betas to global growth and monetary policy pricing as OAT-Bund spreads widened beyond fundamentals. EUR/GBP, EUR HY and French 10Y sit at the bottom of the residual ranking.
Defensives, quality and Value outperformed their growth- and policy-implied returns and buffered broad equities against the Tech-driven momentum unwind.

Each asset's sensitivity to semiconductor stocks explains 54% (R-squared) of cross-asset moves over the past three weeks. Korea and Taiwan equity, US Momentum, Technology and EM equity fell hardest. US low vol, TIPS, staples and long bonds held up.
Sensitivity to crude explains only 2% of the same moves, with WTI still above $100. The dollar behaved in a more pro-cyclical fashion, selling off with risk.

Options price more uncertainty over the next 2 weeks than the subsequent month. This week Nasdaq prices about 1.3x the following month's implied vol, with Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon reporting and the Fed, BoJ and ECB deciding. Next week long-dated USTs and HY credit price bigger moves around the US midterms, with HYG implied vol for the week ending Nov 6 almost 1.3x the subsequent month.
Goldman economists expect a Fed hold on Wednesday followed by a hike in December.

Goldman remains modestly pro-risk: overweight equities over 3 and 12 months, underweight credit, overweight cash over 3 months and overweight bonds over 12 months. Its case for stocks is earnings support, lighter positioning and lower valuations into year-end.

Goldman's valuation table has the S&P 500 at 18.6x forward earnings, down a full turn in three months, near the 47th percentile of its 10-year range. US, German and UK 10Y yields are at the 1st percentile on Goldman's expensiveness scale.
US HY spreads at 337bp are through the 335bp March 2026 peak that Goldman credit strategist Amanda Lynam had set as her downside scenario. IG at 89bp is 4bp from her 93bp bear case.

Goldman forecasts S&P 500 at 8,000 in 3 months and 8,700 in 12 months (+15% total return), WTI falling from $110 to $80 in 3 months (WTI closed around $102 on the day), and gold at $4,715 from roughly $4,000.

Monday brought a relief rally after Anthropic's S-1 and Meta's $35 billion equity raise. Nasdaq outperformed and hyperscaler CDS tightened modestly. Goldman's trading floor described activity as 4 out of 10 with a 3% sell skew and tech supply.
The article's author (Zero Hedge, not Goldman) expects credit to drag the RAI to -1 before a proper buy signal appears, and notes there is no central bank put with the Fed eyeing a December hike.
